q1: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2: SELECT PROJECT_ID, ROUND(SUM(EXPERIENCE_YEARS)/COUNT(NAME),2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT P JOIN EMPLOYEE E ON P.EMPLOYEE_ID=E.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY PROJECT_ID ORDER BY PROJECT_ID

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because they use different aggregation functions. Q1 uses AVG(), which calculates the average of all values in the group, while Q2 uses SUM() divided by COUNT(), which calculates the average by summing all values and dividing by the number of non-NULL values in the group.
counterexample_dsp: The difference between Q1 and Q2 can be observed when there are NULL values in the EXPERIENCE_YEARS column of the EMPLOYEE table. Q1 will still consider NULL values in its average calculation, while Q2 will exclude them from the count, leading to a different result.
